\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اسکی} (eski)}{اسکی (eski)}]{\fa{اسکی} (eski) — skiing; a ski}

\label{lesson:FA-C511-eski}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to have a good time, then the Persian for to become a member.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اسکی}}
\textbf{\fa{اسکی}} (\emph{eski}) — \textquotedblleft{}skiing; a ski\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{زمستانها} \fa{برای} \fa{اسکی} \fa{به} \fa{کوه} \fa{میرویم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zemestânhâ barâ-ye eski be kuh miravim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In winter we go to the mountains to ski.
\end{quote}

\emph{eski kardan} — to ski. Persian puts \emph{e-} before the \emph{sk-} cluster.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{eski} was borrowed from French \emph{ski}, which EtymDB traces to Norwegian \emph{ski} and Old Norse \emph{skíð}, 'stick of wood, snowshoe' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eski}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eski}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{eski}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to have a good time, then the Persian for to become a member, then say \emph{eski} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{اسکی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Skiing; a ski\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{چادر} \fa{زدن} (châdor zadan)}{چادر زدن (châdor zadan)}]{\fa{چادر} \fa{زدن} (châdor zadan) — to pitch a tent, to camp}

\label{lesson:FA-C511-chador-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to become a member, then the Persian for skiing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{چادر} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{چادر} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{châdor zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to pitch a tent, to camp\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ما} \fa{کنار} \fa{رودخانه} \fa{چادر} \fa{زدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâ kenâr-e rudkhâne châdor zadim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We pitched a tent by the river.
\end{quote}

\emph{châdor} 'tent; veil' + \emph{zadan} 'to strike'; present stem \emph{zan-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{châdor} is inherited: EtymDB traces it to Middle Persian \emph{čādur}, 'sheet, veil' (EtymDB). A tent is a sheet you pitch, and \emph{zadan}, 'to strike', is inherited too.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{châdor zadan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{châdor zadan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{châdor zadan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to become a member, then the Persian for skiing, then say \emph{châdor zadan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{چادر} \fa{زدن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pitch a tent, to camp\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اسب} \fa{سواری} (asb savâri)}{اسب سواری (asb savâri)}]{\fa{اسب} \fa{سواری} (asb savâri) — horse riding}

\label{lesson:FA-C511-asb-savari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for skiing, then the Persian for to pitch a tent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اسب} \fa{سواری}}
\textbf{\fa{اسب} \fa{سواری}} (\emph{asb savâri}) — \textquotedblleft{}horse riding\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{روستا} \fa{اسب} \fa{سواری} \fa{یاد} \fa{گرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u dar rustâ asb savâri yâd gereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She learned to ride in the village.
\end{quote}

\emph{asb} 'horse' + \emph{savâri} 'riding' (\emph{savâr} 'mounted').

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{asb savâri} is built on two native words. \emph{asb}, 'horse', is inherited, and EtymDB lists Latin \emph{equus} and Greek \emph{hippos} as cousins (EtymDB); \emph{savâri} is built on \emph{savâr}, 'mounted'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{asb savâri}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{asb savâri}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{asb savâri}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for skiing, then the Persian for to pitch a tent, then say \emph{asb savâri} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{اسب} \fa{سواری} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Horse riding\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پیاده} \fa{روی} (piyâde ravi)}{پیاده روی (piyâde ravi)}]{\fa{پیاده} \fa{روی} (piyâde ravi) — walking (for exercise), a walk}

\label{lesson:FA-C511-piyade-ravi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to pitch a tent, then the Persian for horse riding.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پیاده} \fa{روی}}
\textbf{\fa{پیاده} \fa{روی}} (\emph{piyâde ravi}) — \textquotedblleft{}walking (for exercise), a walk\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدربزرگم} \fa{هر} \fa{صبح} \fa{پیاده} \fa{روی} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedarbozorgam har sobh piyâde ravi mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather goes walking every morning.
\end{quote}

\emph{piyâde} 'on foot' + \emph{ravi} 'going'. Not \emph{piyâderow}, the pavement.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{piyâde ravi} is built on native Persian parts: \emph{piyâde}, 'on foot', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian (EtymDB), and \emph{ravi}, from \emph{rav-}, the present stem of \emph{raftan}, 'to go'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{piyâde ravi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{piyâde ravi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to pitch a tent, then the Persian for horse riding, then say \emph{piyâde ravi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قایقرانی} (qâyeqrâni)}{قایقرانی (qâyeqrâni)}]{\fa{قایقرانی} (qâyeqrâni) — rowing, boating}

\label{lesson:FA-C511-qayeqrani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for horse riding, then the Persian for walking.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قایقرانی}}
\textbf{\fa{قایقرانی}} (\emph{qâyeqrâni}) — \textquotedblleft{}rowing, boating\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تابستان} \fa{در} \fa{دریاچه} \fa{قایقرانی} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tâbestân dar daryâche qâyeqrâni kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In summer we went boating on the lake.
\end{quote}

\emph{qâyeq} 'boat' + \emph{rân} 'driving' (stem of \emph{rândan}) + \emph{-i}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qâyeqrâni} is built in Persian on \emph{qâyeq}, 'boat', a loan usually traced to Turkic \emph{qayıq}, and \emph{rân}, the stem of inherited \emph{rândan}, 'to drive'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qâyeqrâni}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qâyeqrâni}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{qâyeqrâni}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for horse riding, then the Persian for walking, then say \emph{qâyeqrâni} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
